resources.string: Status: standard administrator only — still removable
Android does not let an app become Device Owner by tapping a button. Complete the provisioning below using a computer. On some devices, a factory reset is the only path the system accepts.
Back up your data. If Android refuses the provisioning, you may need to reset the device.
Temporarily remove all Google, Samsung and other manufacturer accounts, secondary users and work profiles. Keep only the main user.
Enable Developer options and USB debugging for the provisioning only. Connect the phone to the computer and accept the RSA key.
Install ADB on the computer and confirm FocusGuard is already installed on the main user. Run “adb devices” and check that the device shows up as authorized.
In the computer terminal, run exactly this command:
When “Success” appears, tap “Verify now”. You can then add your accounts back and disable USB debugging; FocusGuard will not block USB or ADB.

“Already has a device owner”: remove the existing Device Owner first. “Accounts on the device”: remove all accounts and profiles. “Not allowed” or device already set up: back up, reset the device, install FocusGuard before adding accounts and try again. Do not run the command with a package ID different from the one shown above.
Android has confirmed FocusGuard as Device Owner. Hardening is armed automatically while an effective block is running and released only according to the maintenance policy.
